thread.title: Springfield Memorial Hospital accredited as a Level 4 Epilepsy Center
thread.title_full: Springfield Memorial Hospital accredited as a Level 4 Epilepsy Center

author: Y. M. Perkins
title: Springfield Memorial Hospital accredited as a Level 4 Epilepsy Center
text:
Springfield Memorial Hospital has earned a three-year accreditation as a Level 4 Epilepsy Center from the National Association of Epilepsy Centers for the years 2026 to 2028, according to a May 1 announcement.
The accreditation is significant because it recognizes the hospital’s ability to provide advanced testing and treatment for individuals with drug-resistant or difficult-to-manage seizures. This designation highlights Springfield Memorial Hospital’s capacity to deliver comprehensive care and utilize advanced technology in epilepsy detection and treatment.
“This Level 4 designation means our team performs the most advanced testing and provides wide‑ranging treatment and support for individuals living with drug‑resistant or difficult‑to‑manage seizures,” said Christopher McDowell, MD, interim chair for SIU Department of Neurology. “This designation affirms our commitment to delivering advanced and comprehensive care for patients and providing the most advanced technology to detect and treat epilepsy.”
The hospital’s team works in partnership with SIU Medicine, bringing together specialists in neurology, neurosurgery, neuropsychology, epilepsy-trained nurses, mid-level providers, pharmacists, social workers, and other clinical staff. Services offered include diagnosis of epilepsy and seizures, imaging procedures such as intracranial EEGs, management of medication withdrawal related to epilepsy treatments, neuropsychology assessments, neurosurgery options, physical therapy rehabilitation programs, presurgical evaluations for potential surgical candidates, psychiatric services related to seizure disorders as well as routine EEGs. The center also treats neurological dysfunctions including language difficulties or sensory disturbances like numbness or tingling.
The National Association of Epilepsy Centers’ accreditation process involves an independent review that evaluates personnel qualifications, available technology at the center’s disposal, safety protocols followed by staff members during patient care delivery processes along with actual patient outcomes achieved over time. This recognition underscores both the expertise present within Springfield Memorial Hospital’s multidisciplinary team dedicated specifically towards managing epileptic conditions while also reinforcing its status regionally among families seeking up-to-date advancements in seizure care.
